# velero-crds

<!-- GENERATED by tooling/crdgen. Do not edit. -->

CustomResourceDefinitions for Velero (backups, restores, schedules, locations, data movers).

CRDs are copied verbatim from [vmware-tanzu/velero](https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/velero)
at tag [`v1.18.4`](https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/velero/tree/v1.18.4) (commit `4ee1e79a7aed367fd9b767b8219ec65bd0c96892`),
path(s) `config/crd`, and rendered as regular Helm templates so that
`helm upgrade` updates them (Helm's own `crds/` directory never upgrades).

## Install

```sh
helm install velero oci://ghcr.io/spnngl/charts/velero-crds --version <version>
```

Chart `version` equals the upstream version it ships; `appVersion` is always the exact upstream version.
Installing requires Kubernetes >=1.16.0.

### Already have these CRDs?

If the CRDs were installed by the operator chart or `kubectl apply`, Helm refuses with
"rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists". Either let Helm adopt them:

```sh
helm install velero oci://ghcr.io/spnngl/charts/velero-crds --version <version> --take-ownership   # Helm >= 3.17
```

or, on older Helm, hand them over first (replace `<release>` and `<namespace>`):

```sh
kubectl annotate crd backuprepositories.velero.io backups.velero.io backupstoragelocations.velero.io datadownloads.velero.io datauploads.velero.io deletebackuprequests.velero.io downloadrequests.velero.io podvolumebackups.velero.io podvolumerestores.velero.io restores.velero.io schedules.velero.io serverstatusrequests.velero.io volumesnapshotlocations.velero.io \
  meta.helm.sh/release-name=<release> meta.helm.sh/release-namespace=<namespace> --overwrite
kubectl label crd backuprepositories.velero.io backups.velero.io backupstoragelocations.velero.io datadownloads.velero.io datauploads.velero.io deletebackuprequests.velero.io downloadrequests.velero.io podvolumebackups.velero.io podvolumerestores.velero.io restores.velero.io schedules.velero.io serverstatusrequests.velero.io volumesnapshotlocations.velero.io \
  app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm --overwrite
```
